Catalog now 64 scenes.

scenes.title_en: The Gen 9 charter: blood demanded from every beast and every man
scenes.facts_en: מיד כל חיה אדרשנו ('from every beast I will demand it') — the animal itself answerable for human blood; שפך דם האדם באדם דמו ישפך ('who sheds man's blood, by man his blood is shed') for man.
scenes.narrative_outcome_en: Charter, not case — the demand exists from the flood on.
scenes.expect_en: Foundation: pre-Sinai goring scenes may run in Gen-9 mode (demand yes, 30-shekel tariff no).
scenes.replay_state_en: Writes the world's first standing liability rule; every later beast-kills-man event consults it.

scenes.title_en: Cain and Lemekh: vengeance tariffs before law
scenes.facts_en: First homicide; no court exists; God imposes exile + a protective sevenfold-vengeance mark; Lemekh self-escalates to seventy-seven.
scenes.narrative_outcome_en: Killer protected from blood-avengers; escalation spiral until the flood.
scenes.expect_en: NO-VERDICT-IN-TEXT for the statute (pre-law); the sevenfold constant is the tariff idea unregulated — Prov 6:31 later domesticates it to the thief.
scenes.replay_state_en: Consults nothing; writes the pre-law vengeance baseline the statute will replace with courts.

scenes.title_en: Abimelech legislates with the capital formula
scenes.facts_en: A Philistine king decrees: 'who touches this man or his wife מות יומת (shall surely die).'
scenes.narrative_outcome_en: Protective decree; no execution follows.
scenes.expect_en: Comparative: the statute's own capital formula in a gentile king's mouth, pre-Sinai.
scenes.replay_state_en: None.

scenes.title_en: Hagar: the maidservant cast out
scenes.facts_en: בן האמה ('the son of the maidservant') expelled with bread and water; no redemption, no maintenance settlement.
scenes.narrative_outcome_en: God ratifies the expulsion for Isaac's sake but hears the boy; Ishmael made a nation.
scenes.expect_en: DIVERGE under the statute's amah protections (typology mode — statute not yet given); gork fixture already encodes this tension.
scenes.replay_state_en: Pre-Sinai; typology only.

scenes.title_en: Jacob under Laban: wages, gratis-service, theft verdict, guardian's loss
scenes.facts_en: Laban invokes the wage principle ('should you serve me חנם — for nothing?'); the daughters say 'he SOLD us' (מכר); Rachel steals (גנב) the teraphim; Jacob issues a rash capital verdict on the unknown thief ('with whomever you find your gods — he shall not live'); Jacob's shepherd speech: 'stolen by day or night — I bore the loss.'
scenes.narrative_outcome_en: Search finds nothing (Rachel sits on them); the verdict hangs (midrash: it lands on Rachel); Jacob's guardian practice EXCEEDS the forward statute (a shomer does not pay for armed robbery/night theft he could not prevent).
scenes.expect_en: DIVERGE ×2: theft is payable, never capital (21:37 vs Jacob's verdict); Jacob's self-imposed guardian liability is stricter than 22:11-12. Six-plus-years service with changed wages = the term-law's world before the term-law.
scenes.replay_state_en: Writes: teraphim ownership contested; Rachel's status; the fourteen+six service years.

scenes.title_en: Joseph in the pit: the open בור with no water
scenes.facts_en: והבור רק אין בו מים ('the pit was empty, no water in it') — an open pit, a person cast in by its effective owners; Joseph later: 'they put me in the בור' (40:15), drawn from the בור to Pharaoh (41:14).
scenes.narrative_outcome_en: No court; the brothers judge themselves decades later ('we are guilty over our brother').
scenes.expect_en: NO-VERDICT-IN-TEXT + statute lens: 21:33 covers an OX or DONKEY falling in — a PERSON in the pit has no money remedy (block-3 scan: the pit-digger pays for beasts, Heaven judges for men — the 9/10-handbreadth doctrine's moral remainder). The text runs the Heaven-court branch.
scenes.replay_state_en: Writes: Joseph sold-state begins; brothers carry blood-guilt state consulted at Gen 42:21-22.

scenes.title_en: Joseph sold: kidnap, sale, and 'I was stolen'
hooks: 21:16 kidnap (גנב איש ומכרו — steals a MAN and sells him: capital)
scenes.facts_en: גנב גנבתי מארץ העברים ('I was surely STOLEN from the land of the Hebrews' — Joseph pleads the kidnap clause verbatim); brothers sell for 20 silver; Potiphar buys; Ps 105:17 לעבד נמכר יוסף ('sold as a slave').
scenes.narrative_outcome_en: No human court ever tries the brothers; the tradition's ledger (B26 Bahya): the stolen LAMB (Joseph) was repaid four ways — 400 Egypt years, four kingdoms.
scenes.expect_en: Statute lens: 21:16 makes this CAPITAL (man-theft + sale + found in hand). The text's remedy runs through providence ('you intended evil; God intended good') — the flagship NO-HUMAN-VERDICT case; the 20-silver price seeds 21:32's thirty (block-1 scan: the tariff outgrows Joseph's price).
scenes.replay_state_en: Writes: Joseph slave-status (consulted through Gen 39-41 until manumission-by-Pharaoh), Egypt sojourn clock starts.

scenes.title_en: The goblet plant: three theft-verdicts graded, and Judah's תחת offer
scenes.facts_en: Brothers propose DEATH for the thief + slavery for all; the steward grades it down: 'the one found with it becomes my slave, you are clear'; Joseph again: 'only the man in whose hand the goblet was FOUND (נמצא — the statute's own idiom) is my slave'; Judah offers himself תחת הנער ('in place of the lad').
scenes.narrative_outcome_en: No one enslaved; the plant dissolves in the recognition scene.
scenes.expect_en: The scene ARGUES the statute's scale: theft is not capital (against the brothers' offer), collective liability is refused, sale-for-theft only against the actual taker — Egyptian court converging on 21:37/22:2's gradation. Judah's substitution runs the תחת operator on a person.
scenes.replay_state_en: Consults: silver-returned state from the first descent; writes: Judah's surety bond (ערבון ('pledge') state from 43:9).

scenes.title_en: Moses strikes the Egyptian: the mens-rea fork before the statute
scenes.facts_en: The Egyptian is STRIKING (מכה) a Hebrew; Moses looks both ways (deliberation? checking witnesses? — the classic mens-rea crux), strikes (ויך) and kills, hides the body; next day: 'who made you judge (שפט) over us?'; Pharaoh seeks to kill him; Moses flees.
scenes.narrative_outcome_en: Flight to Midian — the refuge pattern (flee, dwell, return on the claimant-king's death: 'the men seeking your life are dead' = Num 35's high-priest-death release shape).
scenes.expect_en: Statute lens: defense-of-the-beaten vs premeditation turns on the two glances; Pharaoh's court treats it as 21:14 (take him even from...); the narrative runs the FLIGHT branch and even the RELEASE-ON-DEATH clock. Pre-statute typology at its densest.
scenes.replay_state_en: Writes: Moses fugitive-state; released at Exod 4:19 by the seeker's death — a replay state-transition the statute later codifies.

scenes.title_en: 'Will they not stone us?' — the stoning verb in Egypt
scenes.facts_en: Sacrificing Egypt's god-animal before Egyptians → ולא יסקלנו ('will they not stone us?').
scenes.narrative_outcome_en: Rhetorical; ledgered in the block-3 tanakh close.
scenes.expect_en: Lexicon witness: stoning as the mob/execution verb the statute will re-route through courts onto the OX.
scenes.replay_state_en: None.

scenes.title_en: Sinai's boundary: the beast that touches the mountain is stoned
hooks: 21:28-29 beast executed by stoning; owner-warning structure
scenes.facts_en: אם בהמה אם איש לא יחיה ('beast or man, it shall not live') — סקול יסקל או ירה יירה (stoned or shot), no hand touching it (the executed carries contagion like the stoned ox whose flesh is banned).
scenes.narrative_outcome_en: The fence holds; no execution recorded.
scenes.expect_en: CONFIRM (structural): the mountain runs the goring-ox protocol AT Sinai BEFORE 21:28 is spoken — the beast as liable actor, death by stoning, no-benefit rule. The statute's first deployment is God's own perimeter.
scenes.replay_state_en: Writes: the warning (התראה) state on all Israel — the מועד ('forewarned') mechanism applied to a nation.

scenes.title_en: The golden calf paid at the ox rate
channels: ch2_digests(B25 Shemot Rabbah 48:6; B26 Bahya; B26 Gra via Pardes Yosef)
scenes.facts_en: The tradition's own computation, triple-witnessed in the tail scan: Moses argues 'You wrote five cattle for the ox' — the FIVE ornament kinds (Exod 35:22) fund the Mishkan as restitution; Bahya: five punishments for the stolen ox-calf; the Gra: 600 worshippers × 5 = the 3,000 who fell (32:28).
scenes.narrative_outcome_en: Levites' sword, plague, the drink, forgiveness cycle, Mishkan built from the payment.
scenes.expect_en: Typology CONFIRM: the nation's own ledger settles at the statute's constant. Pass-2 runs this as arithmetic assertion, not court case.
scenes.replay_state_en: Consults: Sinai warning state (the nation was מועד — forewarned); writes: the ongoing 'day of reckoning' remainder (וביום פקדי ('on the day I reckon').

scenes.title_en: The release patches: Deut 15 and Lev 25 amend the slave term
hooks: 21:7 amah term (Deut 15:12 adds או עבריה — 'or a Hebrew woman')
scenes.facts_en: Deut 15: severance pay (הענק תעניק), the awl (מרצע) restated, 'twice a hireling's worth' clause, woman included in the term; Lev 25: yovel supersedes, 'they are MY slaves' — no permanent human ownership, kin-redemption vectors.
scenes.narrative_outcome_en: Legislation, not narrative.
scenes.expect_en: Patch scenes for the amend-cycle: pass 2 asserts the composed law (term + severance + yovel cap) — the block-1 machine's redemption vectors already encode the Lev 25 join.
scenes.replay_state_en: Writes: yovel clock into the world; every later release scene (Jer 34!) consults the composed rule.

scenes.title_en: The talion/refuge/kidnap patches
hooks: 21:30 kofer — Num 35:31-32 BANS it for murderers (the complementary pair: permitted for the ox-owner, banned for the man-killer)
scenes.facts_en: Num 35 builds the refuge system (cities, avenger, high-priest release) on 21:13's אנה לידו ('God brought it to his hand'); Deut 19 deploys it in the land; Lev 24 restates נפש תחת נפש for beasts (ledgered in block-3 close); Deut 25:11-12 (the wife who grabs) is ch1-anchored at 21:18-19 — the fight clause's own patch.
scenes.narrative_outcome_en: Legislation.
scenes.expect_en: Pass 2 asserts: kofer permitted at 21:30 ⊻ banned at Num 35:31 — the machine must hold both without contradiction (block-3 scan resolved: cofer is for the OWNER's negligence, never for the killer's act).
scenes.replay_state_en: Writes: refuge-city state; high-priest lifecycle as release clock.

scenes.title_en: Lev 19:20 — the designated maidservant misdeclaration
scenes.facts_en: The שפחה נחרפת ('designated maidservant') half-freed case — the block-1 machine already CAUGHT this misdeclaration in its DEPENDS run (state-doc block-1 coding entry).
scenes.narrative_outcome_en: Legislation.
scenes.expect_en: Pass 2 regression-asserts the machine's existing Lev 19:20 catch against the patch text.
scenes.replay_state_en: None (status taxonomy).

scenes.title_en: Rahab's pledge: 'our life תחת yours to die'
scenes.facts_en: נפשנו תחתיכם למות — the spies put their own lives 'in place of' hers; the tradition anchors it at the talion clause.
scenes.narrative_outcome_en: Honored at Jericho's fall.
scenes.expect_en: Lexicon witness for the תחת operator as substitution-of-persons (block-2 scan: תחת = damages semantics, and here voluntary suretyship).
scenes.replay_state_en: Writes: the scarlet-cord covenant state, consulted Josh 6.

scenes.title_en: Achan: Israel STEALS, and his oxen are stoned with him
scenes.facts_en: וגם גנבו ('they have even STOLEN') — God indicts the nation with the statute's verb; sentence executed on Achan AND שורו וחמרו ('his ox and his donkey') — stoned and burned with him (7:24-25).
scenes.narrative_outcome_en: Collective guilt lifts after execution; the valley named Achor.
scenes.expect_en: DIVERGE, doubly: theft is payable not capital (21:37) — but cherem jurisdiction overrides (מעילה in the ban = the sacrilege track, not the theft track); and beasts die for the OWNER's crime — inverting 21:28 where the beast dies for its own act and the owner pays. Pass-2's jurisdiction-flag showcase.
scenes.replay_state_en: Consults: the cherem declaration state from Josh 6:17-19; writes: guilt cleared.

scenes.title_en: 'And He SOLD them into the hand of…' — the covenant sale formula
scenes.facts_en: The Judges cycle runs on מכר: God sells Israel to oppressors; Sisera 'sold into the hand of a WOMAN'; Isa 50:1 'to which of My creditors did I sell you?'; Isa 52:3 'sold for nothing, redeemed without silver'; Ps 44:13 'You sell Your people for no wealth.'
scenes.narrative_outcome_en: Every sale ends in redemption on repentance — the release clause always fires.
scenes.expect_en: Typology: the covenant runs the sale-and-redemption machinery of the slave law with God as seller/redeemer; TT B24 used exactly Ps 44:13/Judg 2:14 to prove מכר = domain-transfer without price.
scenes.replay_state_en: Writes/clears oppression states per cycle — the fold's rhythm section.

scenes.title_en: Samson: 'vengeance for one of my two eyes'
hooks: 21:26 eye-manumission (the slave freed for an eye — Samson the bound grinder!)
scenes.facts_en: Blinded and set to grind as a slave; prays נקם אחת משתי עיני ('vengeance for ONE of my two eyes') — pricing his eyes severally, the statute's per-organ arithmetic.
scenes.narrative_outcome_en: The house falls; more in death than in life.
scenes.expect_en: Typology: talion executed extra-judicially against a foreign nation; the ONE-of-two phrasing shows the injury table's itemization living in narrative idiom.
scenes.replay_state_en: Consults: his own slave/grinder state (the 21:26 shape: mutilated slave → release, here by death).

scenes.title_en: Ruth at the gate: redemption procedure executed
hooks: 21:8-9 designation duty (Ruth 3:9 'spread your wing over your אמה')
scenes.facts_en: A working gate-court: ten elders, the nearer redeemer's right offered first, refusal formalized (sandal), acquisition declared with witnesses.
scenes.narrative_outcome_en: Redemption + marriage; the line to David.
scenes.expect_en: CONFIRM (procedure): the redemption-priority algorithm of the Lev 25 join running live; Ruth's self-naming as אמה invoking the designation duty.
scenes.replay_state_en: Consults: land/widow states; writes: the Davidic line the later scenes' kings stand on.

scenes.title_en: Samuel's clearance oath: whose ox? whose ransom?
scenes.facts_en: את שור מי לקחתי ('whose OX have I taken?')… ומיד מי לקחתי כפר ('from whose hand have I taken a RANSOM?') — the retiring judge audits himself against the statute's own nouns; the people acquit; God witnesses.
scenes.narrative_outcome_en: Clean audit; 'you have not found anything in my hand.'
scenes.expect_en: CONFIRM: the statute as the JUDGE's own liability table — the ox and the kofer as the two canonical corruption vectors (Amos 5:12's indictment is this audit failed).
scenes.replay_state_en: Consults: Samuel's judgeship record; writes: monarchy-transition covenant state.

scenes.title_en: Abigail stops David's self-help vengeance
scenes.facts_en: David marches to kill a household over an insult; Abigail: והושע ידך לך ('saving yourself with your own hand') is the sin — leave the claim to God/court; Nabal dies by Heaven ten days later.
scenes.narrative_outcome_en: David blesses her for the restraint; marries her after Nabal's death.
scenes.expect_en: CONFIRM (doctrine): the statute's deepest premise — vengeance monopolized away from the wronged party (Deut 32:35 לי נקם 'vengeance is Mine') — argued and won inside a narrative.
scenes.replay_state_en: Writes: David's clean-hands state, cited at 25:39.

scenes.title_en: 'His father's house free in Israel'
scenes.facts_en: The champion's prize: יעשה חפשי — the king will make the victor's house FREE (of levies/service).
scenes.narrative_outcome_en: David wins; the promise haunts the Saul-David plot.
scenes.expect_en: Lexicon: חפשי as release-from-service in royal-law register — the manumission word migrated to taxation.
scenes.replay_state_en: Writes: the unpaid royal promise (consulted in David's rise).

scenes.title_en: Nathan's parable: David sentences himself to the four-sheep tariff
hooks: 21:22 the pregnant woman in the story's shadow (2Sam 11:5 הרה)
scenes.facts_en: The rich man takes the poor man's one ewe-lamb (כבשה); David rules: בן מות ('deserves death') for the cruelty AND ואת הכבשה ישלם ארבעתים ('he repays the lamb FOURFOLD') — the statute's exact constant; Nathan: אתה האיש ('you are the man'); Kiddushin 43a runs the agency clause here: אותו הרגת ('HIM you killed') — the king's unrefusable command convicts the sender.
scenes.narrative_outcome_en: The four land across the reign: the child, Amnon, Tamar (the dignity-unit — shamed, not dead), Absalom; David's own flesh the fifth by the no-pity din-rate (Maharsha, tail digests).
scenes.expect_en: CONFIRM ×3: the tariff constant, the theft-vs-cruelty severability (money for the lamb, death-talk for the לא חמל 'he had no pity'), and the agency exception — all executed in one scene. THE flagship.
scenes.replay_state_en: Consults: David's marriage/army states; writes: the fourfold debt as PERSISTENT STATE the fold must discharge across four later events — the strongest replay test in the catalog.

scenes.title_en: The Tekoa widow: the avenger vs the last ember
scenes.facts_en: Two brothers fight in the field, אין מציל ('no rescuer'), one strikes (ויכו) the other dead — the exact 21:18/21:12 fight-fatality shape; the clan demands the killer 'for the life of his brother' (the avenger claim); the widow pleads extinction of the line.
scenes.narrative_outcome_en: David swears protection: 'not one hair of your son falls' — royal commutation overriding the avenger.
scenes.expect_en: CONFIRM (fork): an unpremeditated fight-killing is NOT the avenger's due — the king runs 21:13's shelter logic without a city; the fictional case is legally well-formed (Joab built it to type-check).
scenes.replay_state_en: The parable consults Absalom's fugitive state — the scene IS a state-read on the world.

scenes.title_en: The Gibeonites refuse silver: blood has no ransom
hooks: 21:30 kofer grammar (ובמה אכפר 'with what shall I atone?')
Num.35.31 the kofer ban for murder
channels: ch3:surface שבעתים(2Sam 21:9 homograph — 'the seven of them', noted)
scenes.facts_en: Three-year famine = blood-guilt state persisting from Saul's massacre; David: ובמה אכפר — the kofer question; Gibeonites: אין לנו כסף וזהב עם שאול ('we have NO claim of silver and gold') — money refused, seven persons demanded and hanged; Rizpah's vigil; burial closes it.
scenes.narrative_outcome_en: ויעתר אלהים לארץ ('God was entreated for the land') — He answers only after.
scenes.expect_en: CONFIRM of the COMPLEMENT: Num 35:31's no-kofer-for-blood executed in narrative — exactly the boundary the block-3 machine must draw against 21:30's ox-kofer (owner's negligence ransomable; shed blood not).
scenes.replay_state_en: Consults: Saul's decades-old massacre state (famine as the read!); writes: guilt discharged. Replay's longest state-persistence test.

scenes.title_en: Absalom steals hearts: geneivat da'at at the gate
hooks: 21:37 גנב — the theft verb on minds (Tosefta BK 7:3's SEVEN-THIEVES ladder, B24: mind-theft is the TOP rung)
channels: ch2_digests(B24 Tosefta; B27 Yalkut: Absalom stole THREE hearts)
scenes.facts_en: ויגנב אבשלום את לב אנשי ישראל — the statute's verb, no chattel: the tradition builds its deception-ethics on this verse; counter-case 2Sam 21:12 — Jabesh men גנבו Saul's bones FOR honor (theft-verb, rescue-intent), like Yehosheba below.
scenes.narrative_outcome_en: The stolen hearts become the rebellion.
scenes.expect_en: Doctrine: the verb's semantic field mapped — pass 2 asserts the ladder's ordering (mind-theft > man-theft > ox-theft) as the tradition's own extension table.
scenes.replay_state_en: Writes: rebellion state.

scenes.title_en: Yoav at the altar: 21:14 executed verbatim
hooks: 21:14 מעם מזבחי תקחנו למות ('from My altar you shall take him to die')
channels: ch2_digests(block-2 scan flagship; ch2 grep hit 1 Kgs 2:28)
scenes.facts_en: Yoav grabs the altar horns; Solomon's ruling walks the clause: a deliberate killer (דמי חנם — 'gratis blood', 2:31) gets NO altar asylum; Benaiah strikes him AT the altar when he refuses to come out.
scenes.narrative_outcome_en: Executed at the sanctuary; buried in his own house.
scenes.expect_en: CONFIRM verbatim — the crispest statute-execution in Tanakh: the asylum-exception clause applied by a sitting king with the verse's own preposition logic (מעם — 'from BESIDE' it).
scenes.replay_state_en: Consults: Yoav's two murder states (written at 2Sam 3 and 20) + David's deathbed instruction state.

scenes.title_en: Naboth: judicial stoning suborned — and 'you have SOLD yourself'
hooks: 21:37 מכר idiom — התמכרך לעשות הרע ('you have sold yourself to do evil')
scenes.facts_en: Two false witnesses, a rigged fast-day court, ויסקלהו באבנים וימת — the whole judicial-stoning liturgy executed on an innocent; Elijah's verdict returns blood-for-blood on the dynasty; the sale-verb lands on the king himself.
scenes.narrative_outcome_en: Ahab's line ends at Jezreel; 2Kgs 9:26 recalls 'the bloods of Naboth AND THE BLOODS OF HIS SONS' — collateral victims the record keeps.
scenes.expect_en: DIVERGE (abuse): every procedural form observed, every substantive rule violated — pass 2's showcase that form-compliance ≠ statute-compliance; the false-witness patch (Deut 19:19: do to him as he schemed) then runs on the dynasty.
scenes.replay_state_en: Writes: dynasty blood-debt state, discharged at Jehu's purge (2Kgs 9-10) — multi-book state persistence.

scenes.title_en: Zedekiah's iron horns — one event, two witnesses
scenes.facts_en: בזאת תנגח את ארם ('with these you shall GORE Aram') — the goring verb as false-prophecy prop; Kings and Chronicles carry the sentence verbatim — the catalog's clean parallel-account merge case (the plan's open ruling #2 test row).
scenes.narrative_outcome_en: Ramot-Gilead falls anyway; Micaiah vindicated.
scenes.expect_en: Merge-rule test: ONE event, two text-witnesses, zero contradiction — calibrates the merger before hard cases (Araunah's 50 vs 600).
scenes.replay_state_en: None beyond the campaign.

scenes.title_en: 'Your life for his life, or weigh a talent' — the kofer parable
hooks: 21:12 strike-command (the refusing companion killed by the lion)
scenes.facts_en: The guard-fiction: 'keep this man; if he is missing — נפשך תחת נפשו (your soul for his soul) או ככר כסף תשקול (or you shall weigh a talent)' — the statute's life-or-ransom disjunction as a trap; Ahab self-condemns for releasing Ben-Hadad; prologue: the man who refused the prophetic strike-order dies by lion.
scenes.narrative_outcome_en: משפטך אתה חרצת — 'you yourself have decided your verdict.'
scenes.expect_en: CONFIRM (structure): the kofer-disjunction and the self-sentencing pattern (same engine as Nathan) — the tradition anchored it at 21:32's thirty-shekel clause; the talent is the royal-scale tariff.
scenes.replay_state_en: Writes: Ahab's doom state (consulted at Ramot-Gilead).

scenes.title_en: The prophet's widow: the creditor comes for the children

scenes.title_en: Yehosheba STEALS the king's son — to save him
hooks: 21:37 גנב — the theft verb with rescue intent
scenes.facts_en: ותגנב אתו מתוך בני המלך הממותתים ('she STOLE him from among the king's sons being put to death') — the statute's verb, inverted to salvation; Kings/Chronicles double witness.

scenes.title_en: Ripping open the pregnant: the fetus clause inverted in war

scenes.facts_en: Elisha weeps foreseeing Hazael's הרתיהם תבקע ('their pregnant women you will rip open'); Menahem of ISRAEL does it at Tiphsah; Amos indicts AMMON for it — על בקעם הרות הגלעד ('for their ripping open the pregnant of Gilead') — a nations-court charge.

scenes.title_en: Amos: 'they sell the righteous for silver' and 'takers of kofer'

scenes.title_en: Hosea buys her for fifteen silver
scenes.facts_en: ואכרה לי בחמשה עשר כסף ('I bought her for fifteen of silver') — fifteen silver + barley: half the slave-tariff in coin, half in kind; then the designation terms: 'you shall dwell for me many days.'

scenes.title_en: The thief in the oracles: shame, companionship, night-measures
hooks: 22:2 אם המצא idiom (Jer 2:26 כבשת גנב כי ימצא — 'the SHAME of a thief when he is FOUND')

scenes.title_en: Jeremiah runs the burglar clause: 'NOT in the breaking-in did you find them'
hooks: FORWARD 22:1-2 machteret license (the tail's ledgered border verses)
scenes.facts_en: גם בכנפיך נמצאו דם נפשות אביונים נקיים — לא במחתרת מצאתים ('on your skirts is found the blood of innocent poor souls — NOT in the breaking-in did you find them'): the license of 22:1 invoked precisely to DENY it — they killed where the law gives no blood-license. Job 24:14-16 maps the same boundary (murderer by day, LIKE A THIEF at night, חתר ('dig through') — digging into houses in the dark).
scenes.narrative_outcome_en: Charge stands in the covenant lawsuit.

scenes.title_en: Jehoiakim: the king who works his fellow gratis
hooks: 21:2/21:11 חנם — the slave's exit is gratis; the king inverts it: free men serve gratis (ברעהו יעבד חנם)

scenes.narrative_outcome_en: Donkey's burial promised.

scenes.title_en: Jer 34: the release proclaimed, revoked, and avenged
hooks: 21:2 six-year term (Jer 34:14 QUOTES Deut 15:12's composed form)

scenes.title_en: Jeremiah in the pit: the בור as weapon, and the rescuer
scenes.facts_en: ובבור אין מים כי אם טיט ('in the pit no water, only mire') — the Joseph-pit phrase inverted; the princes USE the pit as a slow execution; Ebed-Melech the Cushite raises him with rags-and-ropes care; Jer 41:7-9 then gives the pit as mass grave (Ishmael at Mizpah).

scenes.title_en: Led like the statute's animals: lamb and ox to the טבח

scenes.title_en: The cosmic kofer: none for a soul — except the one God pays

hooks: 21:37 (שורך טבוח — YOUR ox SLAUGHTERED, the tariff's verbs with no thief to charge)

scenes.facts_en: The captured king's thumbs and great toes are cut off in war — as he had done to seventy kings under his table.
scenes.narrative_outcome_en: His own verdict: כאשר עשיתי כן שלם לי אלהים ('as I have done, so GOD has repaid me').
scenes.expect_en: CONFIRM (doctrine-level) — a court pays money for a hand (machine: tachat_payment('hand') → money); the EXACT in-kind measure belongs to the jurisdiction that can calibrate it, and the defendant himself attributes it there.
scenes.replay_state_en: Reads the ideal-measure doctrine; earliest Judges-era attestation of measure-for-measure spoken as law.

scenes.title_en: The stoning of Zechariah ben Jehoiada: execution without jurisdiction
hooks: 21:14 the jurisdiction clock — no seated court, no capital power
21:12 the mezid track lands on the KILLERS
the demand-verb dying declaration: ירא ה' וידרש ('may the LORD see and REQUIRE')
scenes.facts_en: A prophet stoned in the Temple court 'at the king's COMMAND' — no court seated, no witnesses to any crime, the victim the son of the priest who saved the king's life.
scenes.narrative_outcome_en: The dying words invoke the demand-verb — and 2 Chr 24:25 records the collection: Joash slain by his own servants 'for the blood of the sons of Jehoiada.'
scenes.expect_en: CONFIRM — machine: capital_jurisdiction(no seated court) → False, so the 'execution' is murder; homicide_verdict('mezid') attaches to the killers; Heaven's docket completes within the same chapter of Chronicles.
scenes.replay_state_en: Writes a blood-debt on the royal house; discharged five verses later — the fastest divine collection in the catalog.

scenes.title_en: Jeremiah's capital trial: a working courtroom the machine must decline
hooks: FORWARD: false-prophecy law is Deut 18 — not yet derived, the machine has no rule
the trial runs the capital FORMULA: משפט מות ('judgment of death')
precedent citation on the record: the Micah case; the Uriah-ben-Shemaiah counter-case
scenes.facts_en: Priests and prophets demand death for prophecy against the Temple; officials sit at the gate; elders cite PRECEDENT both ways (Hezekiah spared Micah; Jehoiakim killed Uriah ben Shemaiah); Ahikam's hand protects the defendant.
scenes.narrative_outcome_en: Acquittal: 'this man does not deserve death, for he has spoken to us in the name of the LORD our God.'
scenes.expect_en: FORWARD — the machine correctly declines: no Exodus-21 rule covers prophecy charges. Kept in the catalog because a machine that ruled on everything would be a toy; the decline IS the verdict.
scenes.replay_state_en: Reads court procedure (formula, precedent, advocacy) as a living institution late in the monarchy — awaiting the Deut 18 machine.
